To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the UK’s national greenhouse gas emissions inventory is incomplete and that it does not provide a complete and accurate measure of the UK’s contribution to the problem of global warming.

the UK’s greenhouse gas emissions are likely to be 2-3 per cent higher than previously estimated, but that this is not likely to have any major impact on the UK’s obligations under the Climate Change Convention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an inventory system that will be robust, flexible and transparent, and that can be applied to the measurement of greenhouse gas emission levels for a wide range of countries.
the development of an appropriate framework for estimating national greenhouse gas emissions, and with the application of this framework to the UK.
the development of a methodology to measure and monitor the aggregate greenhouse gas fluxes of the UK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need for a more comprehensive and detailed statement on the measurement of greenhouse gas emissions.
the UK’s greenhouse gas emissions in 1990 were approximately 0.5 per cent higher than the 1990 baseline emissions.

the UK has a very good basis to estimate its greenhouse gas emissions, but that there are still many areas where the estimates are not sufficiently robust to be used as the basis of a national policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while the UK is capable of producing a national greenhouse gas inventory, there is a need for further development and refinement of methods and data.
the measurement problems of greenhouse gas emissions are considerable and will require a substantial research effort.
the measurement of aggregate national greenhouse gas emissions is a complex and difficult task and that the problems are not confined to the UK.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single, correct way to define and measure aggregate emissions for a country.
the UK has a relatively low aggregate emission level when compared to the US or the EU.
the scope of the UK’s national inventory should be defined to include all anthropogenic sources of greenhouse gas emissions, but should not be expanded to cover the ‘natural’ fluxes of the UK.
